answer: An agent economy can resist sybil swarms by making influence vest like a glacier moves. Each new agent locks a bond that earns voting weight only slowly, over months. An attacker who spawns a thousand fake agents must freeze a thousand bonds and wait just as long, and proven collusion slashes every one. Reputation then grows like a vine, clinging to verified past work rather than headcount, so no cheap shortcut reaches the summit of influence without paying in both capital and time.
